text:
acme-admin: hey @maya — after our IdP cert update at 08:17 UTC our users started hitting a login loop. We see 400/500 errors on POST /api/auth/saml/acs. SAML tracer shows the Response Destination includes a querystring (e.g. https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs?client=acme). Also our AttributeStatement is empty in the assertion we received. Any ideas?

maya: thanks — can you paste a redacted SAML tracer payload and the IdP metadata URL? Also which users (okta/google/magic) are affected? :eyes:

acme-admin: sending two snippets. IdP metadata is https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml (we rotated certs and pushed metadata earlier this morning). Tracer snippet: ```
<samlp:Response Destination="https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs?client=acme" ID="_abc123">
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>...
    </saml:Subject>
    <saml:AttributeStatement />
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```
Users see: `POST /api/auth/saml/acs 400 recipient_mismatch` in their browser dev console.

liam: quick read — looks like the IdP is signing the Response with SignedDestination==https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs?client=acme and our ACS validation is strict on the Destination field (we compare exact URL from SP metadata, which doesn't include query params). So the SignedDestination mismatch leads to rejection. Also empty AttributeStatement probably a separate IdP config or an assertion filter.

olivia: we just completed the platform-side cert roll for idp-ingest at 08:18:50 UTC. deploy-bot shows metadata fetch returned 200 and checksum changed, but we don't strip querystrings when validating SignedDestination.

deploy-bot: sync job id=idp-ingest-20260317-0819 completed. fetched https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml (200). New cert fingerprint a1:b2:c3... stored.

maya: @acme-admin can you confirm whether your IdP intends to include the `client=acme` query param in the Destination? If not, can you switch to bare ACS URL (no querystring) and reissue signed assertions?

acme-admin: we did the cert roll with our SSO vendor but forgot to preserve the ACS binding template — their template appends `?client=acme` to the ACS. We can change it but need a quick mitigation for production users.

liam: mitigation options (short-term):
- flip the support flag in Admin Console: Settings → SSO → Allow ACS query params = ON (temporary)
- or enable a metadata-accept fallback that ignores querystring during SignedDestination check (we can patch, but that's higher risk)

maya: enabling the admin flag is fastest. If you want we can enable for your org only. Note: this weakens the strict Destination check and should be reverted after IdP metadata is updated.

acme-admin: please enable for org acme-corp. Also we still have the missing attributes — our IdP says they will include attributes on next signed assertion once we update the app template.

olivia: done — I enabled "Allow ACS query params" for acme-corp at 08:35 UTC. Please test now. I also kicked a one-off metadata re-parse to ensure new cert is loaded.

acme-admin: testing now... login flow is back for a subset of users. Attributes still empty for the few we tried, but that was expected until the vendor reconfigures assertions.

liam: temporary fix worked. Follow-ups: I'll open an internal ticket to add a safer validation that canonicalizes Destination (strip querystring/hash) before signature verification, and we'll add an audit log entry when the admin flag is toggled. Ticket: SR-SSO-7481.

maya: great. acme-admin, once your IdP re-issues assertions with the attributes and uses bare ACS, please confirm and we'll turn the admin flag off. Also if you want, we can accept and re-sign the IdP metadata via our federation shim to avoid vendor template quirks.

acme-admin: vendor updated their template at 08:55 UTC — they removed querystring and are including AttributeStatement again. Confirmed end-to-end login successful for 5 test users. Can you revert the admin flag now? :tada:

olivia: admin flag reverted for acme-corp at 09:01 UTC. I also attached the ingestion logs to SR-SSO-7481.

maya: closing the incident on our side, moving follow-ups to SR-SSO-7481 (add canonicalization + audit + docs). Thanks everyone.

sso-ingest-bot: note: recorded metadata change for idp.acme.example at 2026-03-17T08:19:12Z, fingerprint a1:b2:c3..., previous fingerprint z9:y8:x7...

acme-admin: confirmed working for all affected users, thanks again for the quick turnaround!
